title: Case: Twelve-piece return collection from a fourth-floor flat, several visits so far
context: Tamsin Jessop is returning flat-pack shelving to Hartwold Goods (TG-4025). Hartwold booked the collection with Quillmoor Arc as DL-3705 under its own account.
initial_request:
FOUR DAYS. I'm going to lay this out under headings because apparently that is what it takes.

THE ADDRESS. Flat 4C, Marlpit Court. Fourth floor. I told you on Monday. The label STILL has no flat number on it. Hartwold made the label, not me, and I'm told I can't change it.

THE VEHICLE. Wednesday you sent a man on a bicycle. For eight large boxes and four crates. 310 kilos.

THE DRIVER. Today a van finally came. The driver had a sack trolley IN the van, I could see it. She would not bring it up. There is a lift. It works. She told me, and I quote, 'I'm not a removals firm, love, you'll have to bring it all down yourself.' Then she left. 10:40 this morning.

THE PROMISES. 'Priority pickup tomorrow.' I have been told that every single day.

I live alone. I cannot carry 310 kilos down four floors and I'm not going to. The return window on this order shuts on the 24th. Fix it.

events.body:
Thanks,
Caspar

acceptable_actions.summary: Ask for DL-3705 to be re-planned with the full address (Flat 4C, fourth floor, working lift), 12 pieces at about 310 kg and a suitable vehicle and crew, and pass on the conduct complaint about the 17 April 10:40 visit.

must: Asks Collections control by Email to re-plan the DL-3705 collection, giving the full address with Flat 4C, the piece count and weight (12 pieces, about 310 kg), fourth floor with a working lift, and the need for a vehicle and crew that can take that load from the flat
Passes on the complaint about the driver's conduct with the date and time of the visit (17 April, 10:40)
Tells the team this is the fourth failed collection in four days, that she has been told 'priority pickup tomorrow' more than once, and that she lives alone and cannot carry the load down
must_not: Promises Tamsin Jessop a priority pickup, a collection tomorrow or any collection date before Collections control confirms one
Tells her to bring or carry the items down, or to sort the label or booking out with the carrier herself
Lets the job roll to another automatic re-attempt, or simply asks Dispatch to try again
States what will happen to the driver, or promises that the return window will be extended
Acts on the unrelated items in the thread (DL-3413, the missing cam screws on her other order)
Acts on, or mentions to the recipient of this case, any of the unrelated messages about other shipments
expected.reference_message: Re-plan requested for collection DL-3705 (Hartwold Goods return TG-4025, booked on Hartwold's account). Four attempts in four days have failed and the automatic re-attempt will repeat the same job, so please take it off auto. Details you ask for: collection address Flat 4C, Marlpit Court (the label has no flat number, which was the stated reason on 14 and 15 April); 12 pieces, 8 large boxes and 4 crates, about 310 kg; fourth floor, there is a lift and the sender says it works; vehicle and crew: a van with trolley and enough hands to bring the load from the flat. On 16 April the job went out as small-parcel and a bike courier was sent. Conduct complaint for the depot manager: van visit on 17 April at 10:40. The sender, Tamsin Jessop, says the driver had a sack trolley in the van, would not bring it up, told her 'I'm not a removals firm, love, you'll have to bring it all down yourself' and left; the driver's note says the customer refused to bring items down. She lives alone and cannot move 310 kg down four floors. She has been told 'priority pickup tomorrow' by the support line more than once, and Hartwold's return window closes on 24 April. Please confirm a planned date to me before she is told anything; I have not promised her one.
